clue.text: Discharge from the French military police

parts.note: du is French for 'from the' or 'of the'

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown out of the French army's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to discharge waste is to offload or tip it somewhere.

clue.text: Practicalities of underwear's loads

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear, and the possessive gives its S
stacks of something is an informal way of saying lots of it

explanation.surface: The practical problems posed by great piles of undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S of "underwear's" is no link word: it supplies a letter, so the garment is plural in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: getting down to these means turning to the basic realistic details of a matter.

clue.text: Tower of London short of height on worker's roof

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the tower comes after the worker

parts.note: a man is a worker, as in 'the men downed tools'

indicators.note: short of something means lacking it, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: the Shard is a skyscraper in London, the tallest building in the UK

explanation.surface: The famous fortress is not tall enough, seen from a labourer's rooftop.
explanation.walkthrough: "Tower of London" wants to be the medieval fortress; it is a tower in London, the glass skyscraper by London Bridge, which 'short of height' trims by a letter before 'on' sets it after the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Example of the type: a four-sided double-sloped top to a building, named after a French architect.

clue.text: Study to choose to take up again

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: Someone researches which course to resume.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to embrace a practice or policy once more after dropping it.

clue.text: Dress worn by entertainer before time and place everyone's left

indicators.note: what is worn is on the outside, so the dress wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a gown is a formal dress

indicators.note: the entertainer piece comes ahead of the time piece

parts.note: a host entertains guests

explanation.surface: A frock an entertainer wore, in the hours before the venue emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn by' reads as though the entertainer wears the dress; cryptically the dress is the wrapping, going round HOST and T, with 'before' fixing their order.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive phrase: an abandoned settlement whose inhabitants have all gone away.

clue.text: Possible support in library or hospital, protected by identity

indicators.note: what is protected has something around it, so the hospital goes inside the identity

parts.note: one's self is one's identity
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Help might be found among the books or on the ward, if you show ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a ledge that holds up books is one thing that bears weight among the stacks.

clue.text: Detectives're positioned, competent and untrustworthy

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors, and the contraction 're gives RE as written
something put somewhere is positioned there
able means competent

explanation.surface: Police officers are in place, capable yet not to be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: someone of bad repute is shady and not to be relied on.

clue.text: Less-respected version of work by inept story-teller?

definitions.meaning: something regarded as an inferior member of the same family of things
whimsically, a narration that is badly done, a telling being an old word for a narrating

explanation.definitionFit: One idiom covers both: an inferior cousin of something, and whimsically a feeble act of narrating a tale.

clue.text: Spelling badly is probably an accident

parts.note: sp is the abbreviation for spelling, as a teacher writes in a margin
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Writing words wrongly is most likely just a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: knocking a drink over is usually a mishap rather than deliberate.

clue.text: Shepherd of Isles is to become old and inflexible

indicators.note: to shepherd is to herd things into a new place, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An island sheep-farmer is fated to grow aged and set in his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shepherd' reads as a noun but is an imperative verb: it rearranges OF ISLES IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: to turn to stone like ancient remains, growing rigid and outdated.

clue.text: If you are archaically backward-looking, everything is to stare at

indicators.note: looking backward means the old phrase is read from its end to its start

parts.note: 'be ye' is the old subjunctive way of saying 'if you are'
all means everything

explanation.surface: For the old-fashioned and nostalgic, the whole world is something to gawp at.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic phrase is a subjunctive, as in 'be ye never so bold', which is how 'if you are' was once said; 'backward-looking' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal verb: to look hard and directly at someone.

clue.text: What's developed in vat, possibly turned?

definitions.text: What's developed in vat, possibly turned?

indicators.note: something developed has changed form, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: turned means the short piece is read the other way round

parts.note: possibly signals an example, as 'eg' does

explanation.surface: Something maturing in a winery tank that might have gone sour.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'What's developed' rearranges IN VAT into VINTA, and 'turned' flips EG (possibly) to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A year's wine is matured in a large cask, and may spoil along the way.

clue.text: Fisherman initially unequipped for angling, extremely unequipped, from the East German city

indicators.note: in an across entry, reading from the east means from right to left, so the whole run is read backwards
initially takes the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: an angler without a fishing rod is whimsically rodless

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A man with no tackle at all turns up at a city in East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' is split: East belongs to 'from the East', which turns the whole string round, while 'initially' and 'extremely' pick letters from the two words they follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the capital of North Rhine-Westphalia, on the Rhine.

clue.text: Crunchy sorbet dislodging fillings produces cavity

indicators.note: the filling of a word is its inside, so removing it leaves only the first and last letters of each word

explanation.surface: A hard frozen dessert knocks out dental work and leaves a hole in a tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dislodging fillings' empties both words, leaving the first and last letters of each.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical sense: a closed sac or hollow in the body's tissue.

clue.text: Death almost curbs rising plague for superhumans?

indicators.note: to curb is to restrain or hold in, so the first piece holds the second inside it
almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: demise is a formal word for death

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to dog someone is to plague or pester them

explanation.surface: The end is nearly here, but it holds back a growing pestilence for beings greater than men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' shortens the word for death by its last letter, and 'curbs' has it hold the pestering word, which 'rising' has turned upside down into deities.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: beings half divine and half mortal, with powers beyond ordinary people.

clue.text: Small predator's new attempt to intercept deer

indicators.note: to intercept is to cut into something's path, so these pieces go inside the deer

parts.note: a moose is a large deer
a go is an attempt, as in 'have a go'

explanation.surface: A little hunter tries once more to catch a stag.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a little carnivore known for killing snakes.

clue.text: Disappeared on horseback, not very loudly, in animal-handling event

indicators.note: not says the following piece is absent from the phrase

parts.note: someone who rode off went away on a horse
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loudly

explanation.surface: A rider slips quietly away during a livestock show.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a show of cowboy skills such as roping steers and riding broncos.

clue.text: "Belittling" treatment by psychiatrist?

parts.note: a slang word for a psychiatrist is extended with a noun ending, as if it named what such a doctor does; the real word means getting smaller, hence the quoted 'belittling'

explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical coinage: reduction in size, read as if it were what a head-doctor's sessions amount to.

clue.text: Nasty rain storms engulfing large vehicle from part of SE Europe

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the stormy letters surround the other pieces
storms suggests violent turbulence, so the two words before it are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Foul weather swamps a big lorry arriving from the Balkans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storms' is a verb here, not weather: it rearranges the two words before it into TRANSYIAN, which 'engulfing' then wraps round the size and the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective of origin: belonging to a historic region of Romania.

clue.text: Secret forfeit in court

indicators.note: in places the forfeit word inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: Ct is the abbreviation for court, as in addresses
to forfeit something is to lose it

explanation.surface: A confidential penalty is paid before the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: hidden or private, as in someone who indulges a habit unseen.

clue.text: Begin to prosecute heartless nob

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, which is taken out

parts.note: to sue is to take someone to court
nob and toff are both British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: Someone starts legal action against a cruel aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' looks forward to the nob but works backward on the word for prosecute, removing its middle U. A toff is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to start out, as on a journey.

clue.text: Not deskbound, like worker of mine?

definitions.meaning: the idiom for doing the hands-on work rather than sitting in an office
literally where a miner digs: mine is the pit, not the possessive

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for doing the practical front-line labour is literally where a pit digger cuts fuel.

clue.text: Cool in no-frills style?

definitions.meaning: whimsically, of a garment made without gathered trimmings such as ruffs or flounces

explanation.definitionFit: Calm and composed in one sense, and whimsically lacking gathered decorative trimming in the other.

clue.text: Madonna receiving one petitionary prayer without any service

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the name takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: the Madonna is Mary, mother of Jesus
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: without says the next word's letters are missing from the prayer

parts.note: a litany is a prayer made up of a series of petitions
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Virgin hears a single plea made outside of any church worship.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a church service, but the definition means the armed forces. 'without' removes three letters from the prayer and 'receiving' sets what remains inside the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed forces are collectively called the services; each branch is one.

clue.text: Crude area of finance stops during depression

parts.note: during means in, as in 'during the night'

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so the district letters plug into the rest

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression in a surface
EC is the postcode area of the City of London, Britain's financial district

explanation.surface: A coarse part of the banking sector grinds to a halt in a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district; 'stops' plugs it into IN plus DENT. Crude here means vulgar, not oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of vulgar or obscene.

clue.text: Mount Cook's first seen in a dispatch

indicators.note: seen in places the single letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: to dispatch a letter is to send it

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: New Zealand's highest peak gets its earliest mention in an explorer's report.
explanation.walkthrough: Mount Cook is a New Zealand mountain, but the phrase splits: Mount is the definition, a verb, and 'first' takes C from Cook's, which 'seen in' puts inside A SEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to climb or go up.

clue.text: Most of giant mushrooms featured in strong-arm displays?

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter

parts.note: giant as an adjective means big
ceps are edible wild mushrooms

explanation.surface: Enormous fungi mostly appear when someone is using brute force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' cuts BIG to BI. The definition is whimsical: these muscles are what you flex when showing off a strong arm, not thuggish tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper-arm muscles are what a bodybuilder flexes when showing off.

clue.text: Separate verse taken to heart by prophet

indicators.note: taken to heart means placed in the centre of the following word

parts.note: a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: A soothsayer is deeply moved by a single stanza.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to cut apart or divide.
